blocks.text: ABYSSALS PROJECT
CHECKLIST 06
Items, Shops & Economy
LOCKED IMPLEMENTATION SPECIFICATION v1.0
STATUS

COMPLETE / LOCKED at implementation-design level. This document closes CHECKLIST 06. It fixes the routine consumable catalogue, capture-food economy, evolution-item sourcing, held-item role mapping, town-by-town shop progression, trainer rewards, sellable treasure rules, and the Cybressa Trial Mark growth-training economy. Later implementation may tune presentation or fix defects, but mechanical changes require an explicit Checklist 06 revision rather than silent drift.
Canonical creature terminology: Abyssal / Abyssals. Legacy source filenames may still contain older project wording.
LOCK SUMMARY

No resurrection consumables exist. Normal shops use a compact FireRed-readable item economy; wild battles award no money and do not create a crafting-material grind. Capture remains food-based. Standard evolution items have authored guaranteed copies and late renewable access. Cybressa contains The Proven Grounds, which pays Trial Marks for repeatable deterministic procedural contracts; Trial Marks buy temporary +20 percentage-point stat-growth training effects lasting 1–5 future level-ups. Each Abyssal may hold five such active effects at once, all on one stat or split freely across stats.
1. Canon authority and completion boundary

CHECKLIST 01 remains the sole authority for deterministic Fire Emblem-style stat growth, growth seeds, exceptional growth above 100%, HP growth increments and evolution-history handling. Checklist 06 only supplies temporary effective-growth modifiers.
CHECKLIST 04 remains the sole authority for trainer identities, teams, levels, AI, semantic held-item roles and healing-bag counts. Checklist 06 maps those semantic roles/counts to actual item IDs.
CHECKLIST 05 remains the sole authority for Hell Warden native fields. Terrain held items defined here may interact with an active field, but may not change the field payload itself.
The regional dex progression workbook remains the authority for the fifteen existing item-evolution names, source species, targets and minimum levels. Those names are preserved exactly here.
There is no crafting economy, durability system, carry weight, random shop pricing, merchant haggling minigame or routine monster-material loop.
Core medicine access must not depend on SPARE / EXECUTE outcomes. Town state may change NPCs, dialogue or shopkeeper identity, but equivalent essential stock remains available.
IMPLEMENTATION PRINCIPLE

The economy should create choices between healing, capture food, evolution and held equipment without making ordinary progression depend on repetitive money grinding. Specialised stat growth is deliberately moved into an optional repeatable side economy so players who enjoy long-form optimisation can pursue it without making it mandatory.
2. Standard currency, inventory and sale rules

rows: None as a routine system. Scripted quest/relic encounter rewards are authored events, not random material farming.
Ordinary purchasable items sell for 50% of current standard shop price, rounded down to the nearest whole unit.
Sells for its listed full value.
Cannot be sold, discarded, stolen through parley or consumed except by their explicit story function.
Evolution items, held equipment and other unique/rare valuables require a second confirmation before sale.
99 per item ID unless the item is explicitly unique.
No random or reputation-based price variation. Equivalent shops use the same base price.

blocks.text: 3.4 Temporary battle-stat draughts
No X Accuracy or Dire Hit equivalent is part of the standard item catalogue.
These are battle-stage items only. They do not modify permanent growth percentages and are separate from Proven Grounds training.
3.5 Escape and encounter control

Smoke Bomb (ITEM_UTILITY_SMOKE_BOMB): price 400; guarantees escape from an ordinary wild battle. It cannot escape trainer battles, mandatory encounters, Wardens, final bosses or encounters flagged noEscape.

There is no purchasable Repel family. The permanent Resonator remains the encounter-suppression system: when enabled it suppresses generated encounters at least five levels below the lead living Abyssal.
The Resonator has no charges, item cost or recurring money sink.
4. Capture-food catalogue and economy
The Generation III capture formula and shake checks remain unchanged. Food supplies the Ball Bonus / catch modifier.

blocks.text: 4.1 Saint's Banquet finite supply
Guaranteed copy 1: Ramelle — awarded by the city alchemist after the Chapter 9 leader-resolution sequence and before the Old Catacombs descent becomes the active objective.
Guaranteed copy 2: Circle II — awarded at the House of Unfinished Things safe threshold after Ossael is defeated.

Saint's Banquet is never normal shop stock and has no main-campaign renewable source. The three copies above are the complete v1.0 supply.
Its scarcity cannot make a species permanently missable because all species remain capturable through the ordinary formula and other foods.

blocks.text: 7.1 Hell threshold vendors
Hell safe thresholds may sell essentials but do not create a separate inflated price economy.
Baseline threshold stock: Trail Bread, Seasoned Jerky, Royal Feast, Field Salve, Greater Remedy, Grand Restorative, Panacea, Focus Tonic, Deep Tonic and Smoke Bomb.
Threshold vendors use the same prices as mortal shops.
The Proven Grounds and Trial Mark shop remain physically located in Cybressa; no duplicate Hell franchise is created.
Carriage does not operate in Hell. This document does not alter the already-locked Hell transit/backtracking rules.
8. Cybressa special economy — The Proven Grounds

Cybressa market ward contains The Proven Grounds: a repeatable procedural Trial Contract office and linked specialist item counter. Its currency is Trial Marks. This is optional optimisation content, not a main-story gate.
8.1 Trial Marks

rows: Trial Marks cannot be sold or discarded.
Trial Marks cannot be selected or removed by parley-loss logic.
No practical progression cap; use a large integer storage ceiling.
Contract generation is deterministic from save seed + completedTrialCount + rank, so reloading does not reroll a contract.

blocks.text: 8.2 Procedural Trial Contracts

A contract combines one unlocked eligible area, one objective family and one compatible modifier. It never selects a safe settlement, a no-encounter story sequence or an area not yet legitimately reached.
HUNT — defeat 3–5 marked generated wild encounters drawn from the area's current encounter table.
CAPTURE — capture one eligible marked target selected from the area's current ecological table; mythics and finite authored encounters are excluded.
SURVEY — visit 2–3 marked nodes in the selected area; at least one node triggers a marked encounter before completion.
GAUNTLET — win 2–4 marked encounters before returning to an alchemist or cancelling the contract.
Modifiers may change eligible time-of-day table, target habitat/type family, number of marked nodes/encounters or route depth. They may not secretly scale enemy levels to the player.
Contract encounters obey the authored area's normal level ranges and battle rules. Higher ranks use later unlocked areas rather than dynamic player-level scaling.
Cancelling a contract pays no Trial Marks and increments no completion count. Once accepted, its seed and targets remain fixed until completed or cancelled.

blocks.text: 8.3 Growth-training consumables

Each training consumable adds +20 percentage points to one stat's effective growth chance for a fixed number of future level-up events. It does not grant a stat directly and does not change the immutable growth seed or deterministic roll value.
FIVE-SLOT TRAINING CONTRACT
Each individual Abyssal instance has exactly five growth-training slots.
A slot is either empty or stores: statId, modifier=+20 percentage points, and remainingLevels=1–5.
The five active slots may all target the same stat or may be split across any combination of HP, Attack, Defence, Special Attack, Special Defence and Speed.
Example: five active Attack effects = +100 percentage points to effective Attack growth while all five remain active.
Example: 3× Attack + 2× Speed is legal. Example: five different stats is legal.

Using a training item when fewer than five slots are occupied fills one empty slot. If all five are occupied, use is blocked until at least one slot expires; existing effects are never silently overwritten.

On each level-up, calculate that level's growth using base/current-species growth plus the sum of active modifiers for each stat, using Checklist 01's deterministic roll and exceptional-growth resolver unchanged.
After the level-up has resolved, decrement remainingLevels by 1 on every active training slot. Remove any slot that reaches 0.
All active slots tick on every level-up event whether or not their affected stat successfully grows.
Evolution does not clear or reroll training slots. The evolved species supplies future base growth, while the same still-active +20-point slot modifiers continue for their remaining levels.
Reserve storage does not pause or remove training slots; they simply do not tick while the Abyssal does not level.
At Level 200 an Abyssal cannot consume a new growth-training item because there is no future level-up for it to affect.
If fewer future level-ups remain before Level 200 than the item's duration, the UI warns that unused duration will be wasted before asking for confirmation.
9. Trainer rewards, treasure and non-wild income
Trainer rewards are deterministic and derive from the frozen Checklist 04 tier, maximum team level and team size.
STANDARD PAYOUT FORMULA
Let L = highest enemy Abyssal level and N = enemy team size. Round the final value to the nearest 10.
Named story battles may add a one-time authored treasure reward on top of the formula, but do not silently substitute a different cash multiplier.
Ordinary wild battles award no money.
Wardens and cosmic/postgame bosses do not inexplicably pay a purse; their authored rewards may be treasure, relics or unlock flags.
9.1 Sell-only treasure
Sell-only treasures have no battle, capture, evolution or quest use unless a separately authored quest explicitly references a different item ID.
Exploration treasure and finite trainer rewards must be placed generously enough that a normal critical-path player can maintain capture food and healing without grinding.
10. Economy balance and parley boundary
Healing, capture food and occasional evolution/held-item purchases are intended to compete for standard money.

A player following the critical path, fighting a normal share of trainers and opening ordinary visible treasure should be able to maintain baseline Trail Bread / Seasoned Jerky and healing stock without repetitive farming.
Royal Feast, full heals, held items and renewable evolution items are deliberate discretionary purchases rather than assumed after every battle.
The repeatable Trial Contract economy does not generate standard money. It cannot be used as an infinite cash printer.

The exact retreat/parley loss transaction remains Checklist 13 territory. Checklist 06 only establishes eligibility: standard money and eligible non-key possessions may be lost; key items and Trial Marks may not.
Evolution items and held equipment remain eligible for parley loss under the previously approved high-stakes rule, subject to Checklist 13's final algorithm and confirmation safeguards.
11. Implementation data contract
Recommended stable data shapes below are implementation identifiers, not new mechanics.
11.1 Item catalogue fields
id, displayName, category, buyPrice, sellPriceRule, stackLimit, usableInBattle, usableOutOfBattle, targetRule, effectPayload, firstShopFlag, rarityTag.
Held items additionally store heldRole and passivePayload.
Evolution items store evolutionSourceSpecies, evolutionTargetSpecies, minLevel and consumedOnEvolution=true.
Capture foods store catchModifierFunction / condition rather than duplicating the catch formula.
11.2 Shop inventory fields
shopId, settlementId, currencyType, inventoryItemIds, unlockFlag, stateVariantGroup.
State variants may swap NPC identity/dialogue but must resolve to equivalent essential stock.
SHOP_CYBRESSA_PROVEN_GROUNDS uses CURRENCY_TRIAL_MARK only and never accepts standard money.
11.3 Training state
Each Abyssal instance stores trainingSlots[5].
Training slot shape: {statId, modifierPoints:20, remainingLevels:1..5}.
The growth engine reads the sum of active slot modifiers at the moment of each deterministic level-up roll; it never mutates the immutable growth seed.
Training state is instance state and must be serialised in Ironman saves. It cannot be rerolled by reload/action order.
11.4 Procedural contract state
completedTrialCount is persistent.
activeTrial stores rank, generationSeed, areaId, objectiveType, modifierId, targetIds and progress.
generationSeed derives deterministically from saveSeed + completedTrialCount + rank.
Completing a contract increments completedTrialCount exactly once, grants the rank reward exactly once, clears activeTrial and allows the next contract to generate.
